subject: Contract review: throughput uplift + latency guarantees for renewal
messages:
From: Kevin Marshall <kevin@optiscale.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + Service guarantees

Hi Vivek,

Hope you had a good weekend — OptiScale's renewal is coming up in May and we want to align on a couple of items before the renewal deck goes to our finance team. High level: we're planning an expansion (expected 2.5x token volume by Q3) and we need firmer guarantees on latency and availability for latency-sensitive customer-facing features.

Current state: we run on Redwood Hosted with occasional Dedicated bursts; average p95 latency is ~82ms for our production traffic (attached baseline). We'd like to discuss: 
- A dedicated throughput reservation (reserve capacity so we don't see warm-up variability) — target steady concurrency ~6000 RT calls/min
- A tighter latency commitment: seeking 50ms p95 under the reserved capacity;
- Faster incident response and a higher support tier (24x7 Priority/Phone escalation)

Can Redwood provide an outline of options and rough delta on pricing for those guarantees? Also worth calling out: procurement will want an explicit credit/penalty construct for missed latency SLOs (not just uptime).

If useful, I can send our SLA risk assessment and projected utilization profile. Curious if you and your team have a set of standard addenda for latency SLOs + capacity reservations.

Thanks,
Kevin
Kevin Marshall
Head of Platform, OptiScale
procurement@optiscale.com
Attachment: OptiScale_LatencyBaseline_20280315.csv (CSV)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Marshall <kevin@optiscale.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + Service guarantees

Kevin — thanks for the note and the baseline. High-level: we can support a dedicated reservation and offer two latency SLO pathways depending on how prescriptive you want the contract to be. Quick summary below; I'll loop in Laura and Connor for pricing/ops details and a draft MOU.

Options (preliminary):
1) Managed Reservation + Support Pro (recommended)
   - Reserved pool sized to target your 6000 RT calls/min steady concurrency with headroom for 30% burst.
   - Latency: contractual p95 <= 55ms (applies when traffic served from reserved pool).
   - Support: 24x7 Priority phone + 1-hour critical response.
   - Credit: service credit for sustained p95 deviation >5% over a billing month.
   - Pricing: incremental reserved capacity fee + support uplift (I asked Laura for numbers below).

2) Aggressive SLO + Dedicated On-Prem-like Guarantees
   - Dedicated (single-tenant) fleet with extra performance tuning and hot-cache holdovers.
   - Latency: contractual p95 <= 50ms with explicit rollback and escalation playbook.
   - Support: named engineering on-call + weekly cadence during rollout window.
   - Pricing: materially higher; includes dedicated engineering entitlement.

Action items I propose:
- Laura to share pricing tiers and an MOU template.
- Connor to scope capacity reservation lead time and required traffic shaping for a smooth rollout.
- Kevin — please confirm target commitment length (12 vs 24 months) and whether you want the aggressive SLO for all traffic or only a % of production (canary-first).

I can get a draft MOU over by EOD Friday if we have the commitment length.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Marshall <kevin@optiscale.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + Service guarantees

Kevin / team — following up with concrete commercials and a draft MOU (attached). Quick notes below to make the decision easier.

Assumptions based on your baseline + 2.5x growth:
- Effective reserved units: equivalent to ~3x current committed throughput to provide headroom for bursts and warm-cache.
- Ramp: we propose a three-month ramp (month1 40%, month2 70%, month3 100%) so we don't oversubscribe GPU pools upfront.

Pricing (summary):
- Option A (Managed Reservation + Support Pro): +$45k/month reserved capacity fee + $12k/month support uplift (12-month commit).
- Option B (Dedicated SLA – 50ms p95): +$95k/month reserved + $35k/month advanced support (includes named eng on-call).
- Discounts: 10% discount if OptiScale signs a 24-month commitment and prepays quarterly.

SLO credits (proposed):
- If monthly p95 > contracted by more than 5% for >3 consecutive days, credit = 5% of monthly reserved fee per incident up to 20% cap.
- For failures causing >2 hours of sustained degraded latency at production scale, one-time credit = 25% of monthly reserved fee.

Operational items:
- Connor: will need your traffic shape and a preferred maintenance window. Also planning a two-week pre-rollout canary with telemetry hooks to alert both teams.

Attached: OptiScale_MOU_v1.docx (draft), Redwood_Throughput_Pricing_Options.xlsx

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachment: OptiScale_MOU_v1.docx (DOCX), Redwood_Throughput_Pricing_Options.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Kevin Marshall <kevin@optiscale.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + Service guarantees

Thanks Laura — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications/asks from procurement and engineering: 
- Credits look reasonable but procurement wants an explicit 'canary rollback' clause: if the canary shows >10% regression on p95 during rollout we want an automated rollback and a documented external communication plan.
- For the 50ms p95 option, we prefer it be scoped to 80% of traffic initially (canary + phased ramp). Once we validate over 60 days we can expand to 100%.
- We need a DocuSign link for the MOU and a short SLA exhibit we can attach to our internal procurement ticket (they like a single page summary of measurable metrics and credit math).

Can you update the draft with the phased rollout language + canary rollback? Also confirm the earliest start date if we sign by April 5th.

On timing: we can do a kickoff on April 10th if that works for Redwood.

—Kevin
